sections.intro: The slot system allows you to save multiple rolled classes so you can compare them or switch between favorites without spinning again. When you roll a class in the KELAS menu, you have the option to store it in an available slot rather than immediately committing to it. This creates flexibility during your setup phase.
paragraphs: By default, the game provides a limited number of slots—typically one or two to start. Each slot holds one class result, preserving its name and rarity label so you can review your options at any time. To save a rolled class, confirm the store action from the spin result screen; the class will occupy that slot until you manually overwrite it or delete it.

Switching between stored classes is straightforward: open the KELAS menu, view your slots, and select the class you want to activate. The selected class becomes your active choice for that session. If you want to replace a class in a slot, roll again and confirm to store the new result in that slot, overwriting the previous entry.

If you exceed your available slots, you will need to either commit to a class, delete an old slot entry, or unlock additional slots through progression or game passes. Some players reserve slots for specific playstyles or keep a backup class ready for quick swaps between rounds.

Once the round timer launches, you navigate to the house, search rooms for keys and a numeric door code, and work toward the exit while managing your hearts. paragraphs: While you wait for the round to start, take a moment to read the HUD. Your hearts display in the corner and represent your survival resource for the round. Familiarize yourself with the movement controls now, because once the round timer counts down and the house becomes accessible, you will need to move quickly and deliberately. sections.heading: Searching the House: Keys and Numeric Codes
sections.intro: Inside Opah's house, your search has two distinct targets: physical keys hidden in rooms, and a numeric door code you must locate before the locked exit will open. These are separate items — finding a key does not give you the code, and knowing the code does not replace the keys.
paragraphs: On your first run, work room by room rather than rushing toward the exit. Check surfaces, corners, and interactable objects as you move through each space. The numeric code can appear in different locations between rounds, so there is no single fixed spot to memorise.
For a full walkthrough of which locks each key opens, where codes have been reported to spawn, and what to do when a code fails to work, see the MALAM SAMA OPAH Escape Guide.

sections.heading: Hearts, Opah, and What Happens at Zero
sections.intro: Hearts are your health resource in MALAM SAMA OPAH. You begin each round with a set number of hearts, displayed on your HUD. As you explore Opah's house, your hearts can deplete through encounters with Opah, the antagonist who patrols the house. Each interaction with Opah costs hearts; the exact penalty depends on the encounter type and your class abilities.
paragraphs: When your hearts reach zero, your round ends immediately. You are eliminated from that session and returned to the kampung lobby. This forces a restart: you must spin for a new class and begin another round from the lobby. There is no mid-round revival or second-chance mechanic, so managing your hearts strategically—by avoiding unnecessary Opah encounters or using class-specific defensive tools—directly impacts how long you survive each attempt.

Your heart count is always visible on the HUD during the round. Pay attention to it as you navigate; if you see hearts depleting quickly, it signals that your current approach or route is too risky. Different classes may have different heart totals or damage reduction, so the survival pressure changes with each spin. Learning to recognize dangerous zones and when to retreat is part of developing first-round strategy.

faq.question: What should I do first in MALAM SAMA OPAH?
faq.answer: Open the KELAS menu to spin for your first class, then enter the kampung lobby. Wait for the round timer to count down, move toward Opah's house when the gate opens, and prepare to search rooms for keys and the numeric door code needed to escape.

faq.question: How do I start a round and reach Opah House?
faq.answer: After spinning your class, the round timer in the kampung lobby counts down to zero. When it reaches zero, the gate to Opah's house opens. Walk or run through the gate and follow the path to the house entrance to begin your search.

faq.question: How do you find keys in MALAM SAMA OPAH?
faq.answer: Keys are scattered throughout the rooms inside Opah's house. Check shelves, tables, corners, and behind objects. You will need to collect the physical keys and also locate a separate numeric code to unlock the final exit door.

faq.question: Are keys and the numeric door code different?
faq.answer: Yes. Physical keys unlock individual doors or cabinets inside the house, letting you access new rooms. The numeric door code is a separate sequence of digits required to open the final exit door. Both are necessary to complete your escape.

faq.question: What happens when you lose all your hearts?
faq.answer: If your heart counter drops to zero during an encounter with Opah or another hazard, your character is eliminated from that round. You will respawn in the lobby and need to wait for the next round timer to start a new attempt.

While you search, stay aware of your heart count — taking damage during exploration is the most common reason players fail to reach the exit even after finding the code.

Once you have the code and the required keys, bring them to the exit door, enter the code, and use the keys on the corresponding locks. If the door does not open, see the sibling page on codes for a full troubleshooting checklist, including why round-specific codes expire and where the community server posts updated values.
